title: Neurologic deficit: MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia
content: Neurologic deficit A neurologic deficit refers to abnormal neurologic function of a body area. This altered function is due to injury of the brain, spinal cord, muscles, or nerves that feed the affected area. Examples include: Abnormal reflexes Inability to speak Decreased sensation Loss of balance or coordination Mental function problems, such as memory loss or difficulty with thought processing Vision changes Walking problems Weakness of the face, arms or legs Images Nervous system References De Luca GC, Griggs RC, Johnston SC.
